A region in the $xy$-plane is bounded by the curve $y=5{sin}^{2}⁡x,$ the $x$-axis and the lines $x=0$ and $x=\pi .$ The area of the region is
questions.worked_solution:
The area of the region bounded by the curve $y=5{sin}^{2}⁡x,$ the $x$-axis and the lines $x=0$ and $x=\pi $ is 

$$
A={\int }_{0}^{\pi }5{sin}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Let's recall the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the ${sin}^{2}$ term: 

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x=1-2{sin}^{2}⁡x
$$

We can rearrange the above formula as

$$
\frac{1}{2}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)={sin}^{2}⁡x.
$$

We can now integrate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }5{sin}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =5{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =5{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\frac{1}{2}(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(1-\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{2}{(x-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x)|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{5}{2}([\pi -\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )]-[0-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot 0)]) \\  & =\frac{5\pi }{2}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Here, we use the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the ${cos}^{2}⁡\theta $ term, given by

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta =2{cos}^{2}⁡\theta -1.
$$

 

Rearranging, we have

$$
2{cos}^{2}⁡\theta =\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta +1.
$$

Letting $\theta =4x,$ we have

$$
2{cos}^{2}⁡(4x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡(8x)+1.
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(2{cos}^{2}⁡(4x)-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }(\operatorname{cos}⁡(8x)+1-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =(\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8x)+x-\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3})\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =(\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\pi )+\pi -\frac{1}{3}{\pi }^{3})-(\frac{1}{8}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+0-\frac{1}{3}\cdot {0}^{3}) \\  & =\pi -\frac{{\pi }^{3}}{3} \\  & =\frac{3\pi -{\pi }^{3}}{3} \\  & =\frac{\pi (3-{\pi }^{2})}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Here, we use the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta ={cos}^{2}⁡\theta -{sin}^{2}⁡\theta .
$$

Letting $\theta =3x,$ we get

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡6x={cos}^{2}⁡3x-{sin}^{2}⁡3x.
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2}(2{cos}^{2}⁡3x-2{sin}^{2}⁡3x+6x)\text{d}x & ={\int }_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡6x+6x)\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{2}{6}\operatorname{sin}⁡6x+\frac{6}{2}{x}^{2})|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2} \\  & ={(\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡6x+3{x}^{2})|}_{\pi /6}^{\pi /2} \\  & =[\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\pi )+3{(\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}]-[\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )+3{(\frac{\pi }{6})}^{2}] \\  & =3(\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{4}-\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{36}) \\  & =\frac{2{\pi }^{2}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

A region in the $xy$-plane is bounded by the curve $y=2{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+2-x,$ the $x$-axis and the lines $x=0$ and $x=\frac{\pi }{2}$, as shown above. The area of the region is

questions.worked_solution:
The area of the region is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}A={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(2{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+2-x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate this integral, we use the double-angle formula for cosine that involves the ${cos}^{2}⁡x$ term, given by

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡2x=2{cos}^{2}⁡x-1.
$$

 

Rearranging, we have

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡x=\frac{1}{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+1).
$$

Substituting this into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(2{cos}^{2}⁡(2x)+2-x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}[(\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+1)+2-x]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡4x+3-x)\text{d}x \\  & ={(\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡4x+3x-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2})|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =[\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )+3\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{1}{2}{(\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}]-[\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)+3(0)-\frac{1}{2}(0)^{2}] \\  & =[\frac{3\pi }{2}-\frac{{\pi }^{2}}{8}]-[0] \\  & =\frac{12\pi -{\pi }^{2}}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
